subject: general
question:
The following bar chart shows the marks obtained (out of 100) by a student in 6 different subjects in an examination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b010ed7d5558be7b2ff894c4f7aa99d625cdc185a2f0d217ec5259a60e6c993f.png] 

The total marks obtained by the student in S2 and S4 taken together is what percentage more than the marks obtained by the student in S5? [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b010ed7d5558be7b2ff894c4f7
aa99d625cdc185a2f0d217ec5259a60e6c993f.png] 

**Calculation:**

Total marks obtained in S2 = 67

Total marks obtained in S4 = 83

So, Total marks obtained in S2 and S4 = 67 + 83 = 150

Total marks obtained in S5 = 85

Percentage of marks obtained more than S5 by S2 and S4 students = (150-85)/(85)times 100=(65)/(85)times 100

Percentage of marks obtained more than S5 by S2 and S4 students = 76.47%

**Hence, the required percentage is 76.47%.**
